newsitem.title: CANADA: Crestar sees active drilling on new acreage.
newsitem.headline: Crestar sees active drilling on new acreage.

text.p: Crestar Energy Inc expects to drill 150 to 200 wells on Grad & Walker Energy Corp lands over the next 18 months, Crestar Chief Executive Barry Jackson said on Wednesday.

About a third of those exploration and development wells would be drilled in the Mantario area of southwestern Saskatchewan, where the two firms which announced a merger on Wednesday have core operations, Jackson told a conference call.

He said the deal valued Grad & Walker at about C$7.50 per barrel of proven plus half-probable equivalent reserves. Grad & Walker also has about 500,000 acres of undeveloped land, which held the potential for exploration gains, he said.
"Given the upside that we see, given the very attractive operating cost picture and the concentration of the assets, we think that is fair value in today's market," Jackson said.
He said Grad & Walker's C$165 million in tax pools, or deductions, would eliminate cash taxes for Crestar in 1997 and 1998.
Before the deal, Crestar had budgeted C$310 million-C$320 million in capital spending for 1997 and Grad & Walker C$80 million, with C$30 million yet to spend.
Jackson said he expected no change to expenditure levels this year and a likely increase next year, although Crestar's 1998 budget had yet to be set.
Mailing of the offer was expected on Monday and the deal was set to close on July 28.
The expected drilling on Grad & Walker lands would be in addition to about 60 that had been budgeted by the target firm for 1997, he said.

Crestar said on Wednesday it would acquire Grad & Walker, a Calgary-based oil firm that produces about 12,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day, for C$336.2 million plus the assumption of about C$75 million in debt in a cash and stock deal.
Crestar said it would offer either C$13.50 in cash or 0.509 of a Crestar share for each Grad and Walker share.
A maximum of 40 percent of the price would be made up of Crestar shares, Jackson said.
He said the offer was 45 percent higher than the average Grad & Walker stock price in June.
"This is a substantial premium and clearly it allows the Grad & Walker shareholders to realize value today that might have taken some time in the market for them to achieve," he said.

Holding company Grad & Walker Resources, which is owned by founders Stan Grad and Willard Walker, agreed to tender its 15 percent stake to the offer. Officers and directors owning an additional 6 percent have also said they would support the deal, Jackson said.
